mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary policy, leading to decreased corporate borrowing and investment, which negatively impacts S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day SPX returns are positive in >50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) rises, it indicates labor market tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as companies adapt with productivity gains.
failure_condition: If the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year window, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rapid GDP growth (GDPC1) during economic expansion boosts corporate earnings and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is rapid but SPX returns are negative >40% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as supply chains operate efficiently.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises but SPX returns are negative in >50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: CPI exceeding 5% leads to inflation concerns, prompting tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs rise.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 5% but SPX returns are positive >60% of the time, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales (RSAFS) coupled with low FEDFUNDS indicates strong consumer demand and easy monetary conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If RSAFS is high and FEDFUNDS is low but SPX returns are negative >40%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts (HOUST) in a recovery regime signals economic expansion, boosting related sectors and leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but SPX returns are negative >50% of the time, the hypothesis fails.
